_about: Every number here was measured by the code in this repo on the machine described in 'environment', except entries under 'published', which are quoted from other people's papers and tools for comparison. bpb = bits per byte of the original file. Lower is better. Format-aware transforms - SQL dumps, SQLite files, OCI layers - moved to the sql-compression repo on 2026-08-01, with their measurements and refutations.

environment.gpu: Intel Iris Xe integrated (unused - all inference on CPU)

published._source: xz/ts_zip figures from bellard.org/ts_zip; Hutter record from prize.hutter1.net; image/audio from arXiv:2309.10668

harness_validation._about: bench.py's own xz -9 measurement vs the published figure on the identical file. This is the check that makes every other number here credible.

classical_full_files._about: bench.py, whole files, round-trip verified per row.

ptc_evolution._about: Effect of adding a match model and a stride detector to the pure context-mixing compressor. Predicted in advance that kennedy.xls would gain most, because it is a fixed-record spreadsheet and the model was 1-D.

model_comparison._about: llm_ptc, identical 8192-byte sample of alice29.txt, identical coder, LIMIT=1024. Only the model changes.
model_comparison.retired_2026_08_03: RETIRED. Every row ran at LIMIT=1024 on alice29 with an 8,192-byte sample. That was fair for GPT-2 vs SmolLM2 (1024 is GPT-2 maximum, so both sat at a real ceiling) and the 45% model finding stands. It was not fair to Qwen3-0.6B, which was the INSTRUCT checkpoint at 1/32 of its native context on a benchmark the winner had memorised - three handicaps on one row. See model_comparison_2026_08_03.

model_comparison_2026_08_03._about: Supersedes model_comparison, which is retained but retired - see its retired_2026_08_03 field. Every cell here is batched encode, same coder, stated sample size and LIMIT. The old table ran every model at LIMIT=1024 on contaminated alice29, which handicapped Qwen3 (native context 32,768) by 32x and rewarded whichever model had memorised the benchmark.

corpora.alice29.txt: Victorian fiction, public domain since 1865 - in every training set. NARRATIVE, MEMORISED.
corpora.post2026.txt: arXiv paper prose, post-cutoff. TECHNICAL, UNSEEN. sha256 20b192d7...
corpora.post2026_news.txt: Wikinews articles dated 2026-01 to 2026-05, CC BY, post-cutoff, == Sources == boilerplate stripped (it was 20.6% of the first attempt and a citation list is structurally closer to arXiv references than to narrative). NARRATIVE, UNSEEN. sha256 51f5badb...

matched_50757B_limit2048._about: The controlled 3x3. Identical 50,757 B from each corpus, identical LIMIT. Only model and genre vary.

other_points._about: Not part of the matched 3x3 - different sample size (65,536 B alice29 / 50,757 B post2026) or different LIMIT. Do not compare across sample sizes (trap 2).

findings.model_size_pays: SmolLM2-135M -> 360M is -13.0% on alice29 and -12.3 to -13.5% on unseen text, measured at both 2048 and 8192. Four measurements within half a point of each other. That single sibling swap beats the entire context sweep and is ~13x everything hand-built in this repo combined.
findings.base_beats_instruct: CONFIRMED, and it was listed as untested. Qwen3-0.6B-Base vs the instruct checkpoint at identical LIMIT and sample: -16.7% on alice29, -14.6% on arXiv. An instruction-tuned model is optimised for a conditional distribution that is not "predict this corpus".
findings.qwen3_generalisation_REFUTED: Qwen3-Base beat SmolLM2-360M by 12.2% on unseen arXiv prose, which looked like better generalisation. The genre control kills it: on unseen NARRATIVE it loses to the same model by 0.7%. The advantage is affinity for technical prose - Qwen3 trains on far more code and technical text - not generalisation. One unseen corpus in one genre could not tell those apart, and the wrong reading would have pointed a 10-hour headline run at the wrong model.
findings.contamination_penalty_is_mostly_GENRE: The headline claim that unseen text costs ~38% does not survive a genre control. Holding genre roughly constant (memorised Victorian narrative -> unseen 2026 news narrative), the cost is +0.52% for 135M, +5.74% for 360M, and -0.78% for Qwen3-Base - the last is BETTER on text it has never seen. Normalised against xz, which absorbs how compressible each file intrinsically is, all three do better on the unseen file. The 25-30% drop appears only on the narrative -> technical axis. This does NOT show alice29 is unmemorised; it shows memorisation buys no measurable advantage over comparable unseen prose.
findings.qwen3_is_the_genre_robust_one: Spread between best and worst corpus: Qwen3-Base 9.0%, SmolLM2-135M 31.1%, SmolLM2-360M 32.2%. Lowest bpb and most predictable bpb are different properties, and for unknown input the second may matter more.

caveats.genre_is_only_roughly_controlled: alice29 is Victorian fiction and the news file is 2026 journalism. Both narrative, not the same genre. The clean experiment needs post-cutoff FICTION, which is hard to obtain under a redistributable licence.
caveats.xz_normalisation_is_a_proxy: Using xz bpb to normalise assumes it measures intrinsic compressibility fairly across genres. Reasonable, not proven.
caveats.gemma_untested: google/gemma-3-270m is a gated repo and needs a licence acceptance plus HF_TOKEN. The big-vocab counter-test is still open.
caveats.qwen3_never_reached_its_context: Native context 32,768, tested to 4096, still improving (-5.4% from 2048 to 4096 on arXiv). At 4096 the process holds 4.3 GB - 2.4 GB of fp32 weights plus 2.5 GB of logits - against ~2.4 GB typically free here. Memory-capped, not model-capped.

headline_alice29._about: Full alice29.txt, 152089 bytes. VERIFIED round-trip as of 2026-08-03: sequential encode+decode of the whole file at the shipped defaults, which now means LIMIT=8192. Supersedes the 0.940 measured at LIMIT=1024, kept below under superseded_2026_07_31. The 32/34 B/s pair is the first throughput this project has measured on an idle box over a full file - every earlier figure was either contended or inflated by a sample barely larger than LIMIT. Added 2026-08-31: the SmolLM2-360M row, measured 2026-08-23 and labelled 'measured, not decoded' - it beats the headline by 13% and does not replace it, because a batched stream has never round-tripped through the sequential decoder.

llm_ptc + SmolLM2-135M.round_trip: ok - full file, sequential encode+decode, 2026-08-03, LIMIT=8192

batched_encode._about: 16x faster measurement path. Its stream does NOT decode sequentially (float reduction order), but it proved faithful as an entropy measurement: 27 bytes / 0.001 bpb from the verified figure. NOTE 2026-08-03: this comparison was made at LIMIT=1024. The 0.15% fidelity figure is an alice29 figure - see context_sweep.batched_fidelity_revisited.

sequential_bytes_per_s._about: Idle machine, whole file, nothing else running. Decode is marginally FASTER than encode, which settles the open question from the 40,960 B gate.

superseded_2026_07_31.why: LIMIT=1024 was the default until the context sweep showed it was set from a GPT-2 ceiling. Same code, same model, same file - 473 bytes larger, 2.65%.

llm_ptc + SmolLM2-360M (measured, not de.round_trip: NOT VERIFIED. Batched encode, 2026-08-23, whole file. Sits exactly where the 0.939 batched 135M figure sat before the sequential run: a faithful entropy measurement, not a decodable stream. It is charted because it is real and it is labelled because it is not the headline.

contamination_test._about: Identical 50757-byte samples. post2026.txt is prose from a 2026 arXiv paper, published long after SmolLM2's training cutoff. xz is the control: it cannot memorise, so a surviving advantage over xz is not memorisation.

enwik8_ablation._about: 262144-byte slice from offset 50,000,000 of enwik8. Mid-file on purpose: the first 256 KB contains the XML preamble and scores an artificially good 0.811, a 13% bias.

variants.note: measured on the BIASED first-256KB slice, where LLM-only was 0.817

coder_efficiency._about: probe.py. 'raw model' is -log2 p under the model's own distribution; 'quantised' is under the 12-bit probabilities we actually code against; 'emitted' is real output. coder = emitted/quantised - 1. smoothing = quantised/raw - 1, where negative means the 12-bit clamp SMOOTHS an overconfident model and wins.

context_sweep._about: LLM_PTC_LIMIT sweep on SmolLM2-135M, 2026-08-02. Supersedes the context half of negative_results[1]. That refutation swept 256->1024 on GPT-2 and found -0.7%, i.e. noise - but 1024 IS GPT-2 max_position_embeddings, so the flat curve was a model ceiling being mistaken for a property of context. probe.py had SmolLM2 in the same table, still descending at the last point (1.024 -> 0.999 -> 0.990), and that row is the one that generalises.
context_sweep.method: Batched encode - a faithful ratio measurement, explicitly not a codec. Same sample every row (trap 2). WINDOW = LIMIT//2 throughout. NOT RUNNABLE before the WINDOW/LIMIT clamp fix of 2026-08-01: LLM_PTC_LIMIT above the model max either crashed or silently ran a full-window forward per token.

alice29.txt.note: Public domain since 1865 and on every mirror - the most contaminated file in this corpus. Sized so LIMIT=8192 still slides 3 times; the old sweep used 4,096 B, which tokenises to 1,098, so its 1024 row never slid even once.

post2026.txt.note: Post-cutoff arXiv text - the repo contamination control. Never seen by the model.

per_doubling_pct._about: Percent bpb reduction at each doubling. The shapes differ, and the difference is the whole finding.

context_sweep.finding: Context is worth 2.5% on memorised text and 11.3% on unseen text, 1024 -> 8192. The shapes differ more than the totals: on alice29 the gain halves every doubling (1.54 -> 1.25 -> 0.85 -> 0.43) and is visibly converging, while on post2026 the last doubling paid 3.20% against the previous 3.17% - no convergence at all. 8192 is not "enough context", it is simply all SmolLM2-135M has. The mechanism is the obvious one: on memorised text the model recites and extra context is largely redundant with the weights; on novel text, in-document notation and terminology is the only thing it has.
context_sweep.consequence_for_model_comparison: model_comparison measured Qwen3-0.6B at 1.11 bpb with LIMIT=1024 against a 32,768-token native context. If context is worth ~11% per 8x on unseen text, that row is partly a context measurement wearing a model name. GPT-2 vs SmolLM2 was a fair fight - both were at 1024, GPT-2 max - so the 45% model finding stands; the Qwen3 row does not.
context_sweep.do_not_extrapolate: The post2026 curve is still at full slope at 8192, so a naive read says more context keeps paying. There is no more: 8192 is max_position_embeddings, and RoPE extension changes the model rather than the context. Trap 3.

sequential_verification._about: The sweep above is the batched path, which is a ratio measurement and not a codec. This is the same comparison on the path that actually decodes: real sequential encode AND decode, byte-compared. 40,960 B of alice29 = 11,172 tokens - the smallest size that both slides at LIMIT=8192 and clears llm_ptc chatty threshold so a 40-minute run is not silent.
sequential_verification.cross_check: Sequential says -2.55%, batched said -2.51% on a different sample size. The two paths agreeing on the DELTA to within 0.04 points is what licenses using the fast path for the sweep - it was never licensed for absolute figures.
sequential_verification.speed_caveat: TRAP 6, self-inflicted: results.json edits and git commands were run during the 8192 half and not the 1024 half. Encode 70 -> 49 is trustworthy in direction and roughly in size; decode 66 -> 22 is an UPPER BOUND on the cost, with the true figure somewhere between 1.5x and 3x. bpb is deterministic and unaffected. A clean number needs an idle box, and the full-file headline run is the natural place to get one.
sequential_verification.why_decode_suffers_more: REFUTED 2026-08-03, and it was never real. The 66 -> 22 B/s decode drop was entirely contention from tooling run during that half: on an idle box over the full file, decode is 34 B/s against encode 32 B/s - decode is marginally FASTER. The guessed mechanism (KV-cache pressure at 8192) was recorded as not-investigated rather than as a finding, and it would have been wrong. This is the third time in this project that a plausible mechanism for a contended measurement turned out to be explaining an artifact.

full_file_2026_08_03._about: The real thing: 152,089 B, LIMIT=8192, idle box. Supersedes the 40,960 B rows above for throughput; they stand for the ratio.

sequential_verification.ramp_inflation: The 49 B/s encode measured here is inflated 1.53x against the full-file 32 B/s. Same LIMIT, same code: 40,960 B is 11,172 tokens against LIMIT=8192, so most tokens were encoded at a context still filling toward the first slide. A throughput number at large LIMIT measures the ramp unless the sample is much larger than LIMIT - the same species of error as a sweep row that never slid.

context_sweep.batched_fidelity_revisited: The repo claims the batched path is faithful to 0.15%, measured on alice29. On post2026 at LIMIT=1024 it reads 1.331 against contamination_test 1.338, a 0.5% gap - over 3x less faithful on unseen text. The same runs reproduced that test xz (2.844), bz2 (2.809) and ptc (3.225) figures EXACTLY, so this is a real path difference and not a different sample. Quote 0.15% as an alice29 figure, not a property of the path.

negative_results.claim: bfloat16 weights will be ~2x faster because the checkpoint is 16-bit and we are memory-bandwidth bound
negative_results.detail: 64 B/s vs float32's 84 B/s. No AVX512-BF16 on this CPU, so torch converts to fp32 per matmul and we pay conversion on top.

negative_results.claim: the gap to ts_zip is mostly our 512-token context resets
negative_results.detail: Sweeping context 256->1024 moved GPT-2's bpb by -0.7%, i.e. noise. The gap was the model. CAVEAT added 2026-07-31: the second half of the original claim - 'post-slide tokens cost the same as deep-in-window ones' - rested on probe.py's cold_vs_warm, whose warm bucket was invalid. It defined warm as age >= LIMIT-64, but a token's age can never exceed LIMIT-WINDOW after a slide, so warm contained ZERO post-slide tokens in all three swept configs - it was 64 tokens of the memorised alice29 opening. The sweep half of the refutation stands on its own (it is a bpb measurement, not a bucket comparison); the per-bucket half is unmeasured until probe.py is re-run with the fixed buckets on a sample large enough to slide several times.
negative_results.instrument_fixed: probe.py cold_vs_warm, 2026-07-31: both buckets now drawn from post-first-slide tokens only.
negative_results.revisited_2026_08_02: The sweep half is now SUPERSEDED too, and for the same species of reason as the bucket half. It swept GPT-2, whose max_position_embeddings is 1024, so it measured a model that had already hit its ceiling and generalised the flat result to context in general. Swept properly on SmolLM2 to its native 8192: -2.5% on alice29 and -11.3% on post-cutoff text. "The gap was the model" is still right about ts_zip; "context barely matters" was never measured. See context_sweep.

negative_results.claim: blending a match prediction into the LLM distribution will help on repetitive markup
negative_results.detail: Naive linear interpolation measured 2% WORSE. Fixed by mixing in the logistic domain with learned weights, which then gave -1.2%.
It GAINS 5.3% against GPT-2 by smoothing an overconfident model. Against well-calibrated SmolLM2 it is worth +0.05%, i.e. nothing.

negative_results.claim: SSE/APM will help, as it does in every serious CM compressor
negative_results.detail: Neutral at 25% weight (0.918 vs 0.917), harmful at 75% (0.926). SSE fixes miscalibrated mixers; a well-calibrated LLM has nothing to recalibrate.

negative_results.claim: batched teacher-forced encoding is a free 16x speedup
negative_results.detail: 16x faster and byte-identical output, but the stream does NOT decode with the sequential decoder - diverged at byte 253. Valid as a ratio measurement, invalid as a codec until inference is integer.

negative_results.claim: the first 256 KB of enwik8 is a representative sample
negative_results.detail: 0.811 there vs 0.917 mid-file. The XML preamble inflated it by 13%.

negative_results.claim: rewriting ptc.py's hot loops (unrolled contexts, __slots__, inlined helpers, locals) is worth 1.35x encode / 1.41x decode
negative_results.detail: A 2026-07-31 audit measured 1.35x/1.41x and shipped a working rewrite. Re-measured on an idle machine with interleaved A/B (old,new,old,new - so drift and cache state hit both equally) and fastest-of-N: 1.00x encode, 1.07x decode. A coder-only variant (Model untouched) measured 1.03x/1.19x in a monkeypatch A/B and 1.07x decode interleaved. Both rewrites produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output on alice29/kennedy.xls/ptt5/chinook.db and cross-decode, so the correctness claim held and only the speed claim did not. Reverted: a 7% decode gain does not justify unrolling NCTX/NINP in the file the repo presents as its readable reference implementation, and ptc's constraint is ratio, not speed. The measurement lesson is the point - a speedup measured by running A then B is measuring cache state as much as code.

negative_results.claim: the shipped defaults are the measured optimum (README) - in particular the thread count
negative_results.detail: os.cpu_count() was never swept. It is the slowest of five settings tested for the sequential codec: 42 B/s at 20 threads vs 87 at 6, a 2.07x penalty paid on every encode and every decode since the project started - including the ~3-hour full-file verification. The batched path wants the opposite (20 threads, 967 B/s vs 828 at 6), so one global default could not have been right for both.

negative_results.prediction: the lockstep window-slide path works at S>1, since it is the same code the sequential path runs and the sequential path has slid for the project's whole life
negative_results.outcome: REFUTED - it had never executed at S>1, and would have run out of memory when it did
negative_results.detail: Found 2026-08-31 by reading, not by running. _LockPredictor.feed rebuilds the cache with an [S, WINDOW] forward when segments pass LIMIT, and transformers materialises logits for EVERY position unless logits_to_keep is set (default 0 -> slice(0, None), confirmed in the 5.14.1 source). That is S x 4096 x 49152 x 4 bytes: 0.8 GiB at S=1, 3.0 at S=4, 12.0 at S=16, on a 15.7 GB box with ~2.4 GB typically free. Every lockstep measurement so far was 8 KB or 32 KB, where a segment at S>1 is 140-2,221 tokens and never reaches LIMIT - so the branch had only ever run at S=1, where it is the same shape as the sequential path. The first run big enough to matter is exactly the full-enwik8 verification the roadmap calls 'about a weekend'.
negative_results.fix: logits_to_keep=1 on both slide forwards: 12.0 GiB -> 3.0 MiB at S=16. Verified at LIMIT=128 on 4,096 B, which slides 16 times per segment - round-trip ok sequential, S=1 and S=4.
negative_results.lesson: A code path that has never executed is not tested by the tests that pass around it. All the lockstep round-trips were green and none of them had entered this branch.

negative_results.prediction: the logits_to_keep fix will change the format, since a different lm_head GEMM shape reduces floats in a different order - the same mechanism that made compress_batched undecodable
negative_results.outcome: HALF-REFUTED - the streams matched, the numbers underneath did not
negative_results.detail: Predicted the fix would change the format, since a different lm_head GEMM shape reduces floats in a different order. The streams measured BYTE-IDENTICAL at S=1 and S=4. But the underlying logits are not: max |dlogit| ~4e-5 and ~7% of 30-bit probability buckets move. So the prediction was right about the mechanism and the byte-identity is one sample agreeing, not compatibility. Treat it as a format change.
negative_results.how_to_treat_it: As a format change. Encoder and decoder must be on the same side of it. The byte-identity was measured on one 4,096 B sample at LIMIT=128; the divergence that broke compress_batched also did not show up until byte 253.

negative_results.prediction: bigger models lose - Qwen3-0.6B scored 1.110 against SmolLM2-135M's 0.990
negative_results.outcome: REFUTED - three handicaps stacked on one row
negative_results.detail: The losing row was the INSTRUCT checkpoint, run at LIMIT=1024 against a 32,768-token native context, on a benchmark the winner had memorised. Re-run at matched sample and context, SmolLM2 135M -> 360M is -13% at every context on every corpus. Bigger wins.

negative_results.prediction: Qwen3-0.6B-Base generalises better to unseen text - it beat SmolLM2-360M by 12.2% on unseen arXiv prose
negative_results.detail: Adding a second unseen corpus that was narrative rather than technical turned the 12.2% win into a 0.7% loss. The advantage is affinity for technical prose, not generalisation, and one unseen corpus in one genre could not tell those apart. That control cost an hour and would otherwise have pointed a 10-hour headline run at the wrong model.

negative_results.prediction: unseen text costs ~38%, and that gap is memorisation
negative_results.detail: Holding genre constant with a 2026 news corpus, the cost of never having seen the text is -0.8% to +5.7% across three models. The 25-30% cliff sits entirely on the narrative->technical axis. Normalised against xz, all three models score BETTER on the unseen file than the memorised one. Genre is only roughly controlled - Victorian fiction vs 2026 journalism is two narrative genres - and post-cutoff fiction under a redistributable licence is the honest gap.

negative_results.prediction: sweeping LLM_PTC_THREADS for lockstep will find another free multiple, the way the sequential sweep found 2.07x - the default was inherited, never measured, and a [S,1] GEMM is a different shape from the [1,1] the 6-thread optimum was measured on
negative_results.outcome: REFUTED - the inherited default was approximately right
negative_results.detail: Fastest-of-3, interleaved, at S=8 on 16,384 B: 4 threads 350 B/s, 6 288, 8 276, 12 269, 20 205. Monotonically decreasing, i.e. the SEQUENTIAL shape, so the shipped default of 6 sits near the top. The within-config spread (1.29-2.18x) exceeds the gap between 4, 6 and 8 (1.27x), so the top three are not separable at n=3 and nothing should be quoted among them.
negative_results.what_it_was_worth_anyway: The plausible change - give lockstep every core, since compress_batched wants them - would have cost 1.71x. And recording output size per run is what surfaced the thread-count-is-part-of-the-format corruption, which was the real find. A sweep that refutes its own premise still paid for itself.
negative_results.lesson: 'A default is not a measurement' cuts both ways. Trap 9 says measure what you inherited; it does not say the inherited value is wrong. Two of the three costs here were noise, and the finding came from a column the sweep was not designed to look at.

why_not_just_a_faster_zip._about: Whether "universal, faster than zip, much better ratio" is available. Measured on alice29.txt by bench.py. It is not - that corner is already occupied, and bz2 from 1996 already dominates max-compression zip on BOTH axes.
why_not_just_a_faster_zip.conclusion: ptc's ratio (2.606) is already worse than bz2's (2.272), so speed is not even the binding constraint. Context mixing is structurally ~100x slower than gzip in any language because it runs an adaptive model per bit. A C port lands near xz ratio at worse speed: a worse zstd.

thread_count._about: Sweep of LLM_PTC_THREADS on this 20-core box, 2026-07-31, machine otherwise idle and each sweep run back-to-back. Compare WITHIN a sweep only: absolute B/s drifts with machine state (trap 6), the ordering does not. The default was os.cpu_count()=20, which the sweep found to be the single SLOWEST setting for the sequential codec.
thread_count.why: A single-token step is ~210 tiny GEMVs, one parallel region each, and the work is memory-bandwidth-bound - so past ~6 threads you buy fork-join barriers and hyperthread contention, not throughput. One forward per WINDOW is instead a big GEMM that parallelises properly, so the batched path has the OPPOSITE optimum. Both defaults are now set per-path.
thread_count.gain: 2.07x on the sequential codec (42 -> 87 B/s), which is both encode AND decode. One-line change.
thread_count.format_risk: Sequential output was byte-identical at 3 KB across 6 and 20 threads and cross-decoded in both directions, and the 4 KB round-trip is byte-identical to the pre-change run (515 B). But the BATCHED path at 16 KB does vary with thread count (1,990 B at 6/12 vs 1,992 B at 8/20), so reduction order is observable in general. Safe for the sizes tested; re-verify before a long run.

lockstep_encode_B_per_s_S8._about: Swept 2026-08-31 on 16,384 B of alice29 at S=8, LIMIT=8192. INTERLEAVED (4,6,8,12,20 in order, three passes) rather than back-to-back, because trap 10 says A-then-B measures cache state - the sequential sweep above predates that trap and was run back-to-back. Fastest of three. Instrument validated first against the known sequential result: 6 threads beat 20 by 1.66x and 2.31x on the control runs, bracketing the recorded 2.07x.
lockstep_encode_B_per_s_S8.finding: The lockstep path has the SEQUENTIAL optimum, not the batched one - monotonically decreasing in thread count, 4 > 6 > 8 > 12 > 20. The inherited default of 6 was therefore approximately RIGHT, which is the opposite of what the sweep was run to find.
lockstep_encode_B_per_s_S8.what_it_is_not: A 2.07x-style free win. The within-config spread (1.29-2.18x) is larger than the gap between 4, 6 and 8 (1.27x), so the top three are NOT separable at n=3 and no optimum should be quoted among them. Only the endpoint separates: 20 threads is 1.71x worse than 4, and 20's best run (205 B/s) is below 4's MEDIAN (339).
lockstep_encode_B_per_s_S8.the_value_is_the_negative: The obvious change - 'lockstep batches a GEMM, so give it every core like compress_batched does' - would have been 1.71x SLOWER. The sweep's payoff was preventing that, not finding a speedup.

lockstep_decode_pilot._about: Prototype for Long_Time_Tests 4.6, 2026-07-31: S independent segment streams advanced one token per step in a single [S,1] forward, each with its own KV cache, match bank, mixer and coder. Encoder and decoder run the SAME step-major loop, so both execute identical batched GEMMs in identical order - unlike compress_batched, which encoded [1,W] and decoded [1,1] and diverged at byte 253. Scratch prototype, not in the repo.
lockstep_decode_pilot.sample: first 8,192 B of alice29.txt (8,185 B covered; equal-length segments drop a 2-token remainder)
lockstep_decode_pilot.round_trip: ok at S=4, 8 and 16 - byte-exact in every case
lockstep_decode_pilot.verdict: MECHANISM CONFIRMED AND COST BOUNDED. Byte-exact round-trip at S=4/8/16, decode 2.5x to 8.8x. The ratio cost is real but shrinks fast with segment length: 8.9% at 560-token segments, 2.6% at 2,221. The audit predicted <0.5% for the wrong reason and got the right order of magnitude for large files by luck. Worth engineering, on files big enough to give long segments.
lockstep_decode_pilot.why_the_prediction_missed: The <0.5% estimate was extrapolated from the measured finding that post-slide tokens cost about the same as deep-in-window ones. That is a statement about WINDOW SLIDES inside one long stream, where the model still gets WINDOW tokens of context. A segment boundary is a cold start from zero context, which is a different event. (Note the slide finding itself is now flagged - see negative_results - so it was thin ground to extrapolate from.)
lockstep_decode_pilot.next: Re-measure on a sample large enough that segments stay long: the penalty should shrink toward zero as segment length grows, and the enwik8 case (S=16 gives 6.25 MB segments) is the one that matters. Do not quote the 8 KB ratio cost as the cost of the technique - it is the cost of the technique on a file too small for it.

size_dependence._about: The 8 KB ratio cost is a small-sample artifact, and here is the control. Same S=4, same corpus, 4x the segment length. Encode-only for the sequential leg; the two runs shared the machine so their B/s figures are void (trap 6) - only bpb is used, which is deterministic.
size_dependence.reading: 4x the segment length cut the penalty 3.5x (8.9% -> 2.6%). That is the signature of a per-segment cold start being amortised over more tokens, and it rules out lost cross-segment matches as the main term - those would not shrink this fast with segment length. The cost of the technique is therefore a function of SEGMENT LENGTH, not of S.
size_dependence.not_extrapolated: Two points is a direction, not a curve. enwik8 at S=16 would give ~1.7M-token segments, ~770x longer than the 32 KB test, where the penalty should be far below 1% - but this repo has been burned by exactly that kind of extrapolation (trap 3), so it stays unmeasured until someone runs it.

lockstep_decode_pilot._SUPERSEDED: Pilot only. Built for real in llm_ptc.py on 2026-08-03 - see lockstep_decode. Its ratio figures replicate; its size-dependence claim does not.

lockstep_decode._about: Shipped in llm_ptc.py as compress_lockstep/decompress_lockstep. S independent segments advance one token per step in a single [S,1] forward, each with its own KV cache, match bank, mixer and coder. decompress() routes on a header bit (LOCKSTEP_FLAG), so a caller does not need to know which encoder made a blob.
lockstep_decode.why_it_decodes_when_compress_batched_doe: compress_batched encoded with a [1,W] forward and decoded with [1,1]. Different GEMM shapes reduce floats in a different order, and it diverged at byte 253. Lockstep runs the SAME step-major loop in both directions, so both sides execute identical shapes in identical order and see bit-identical probabilities.

invariants.constant_batch_shape: A finished segment keeps being fed a filler token rather than leaving the batch. Dropping it would reshape the GEMM mid-stream and change the numbers for every SURVIVING row. Rows do not attend to each other, so batch content is irrelevant - shape is the thing that must not move.
invariants.equal_segment_lengths: Segments differ by at most one token, so they all cross LIMIT on the same step, slide together, and keep the KV cache rectangular.

lockstep_decode.round_trip: byte-exact at S=1, 2, 4, 8, 16 on 8,192 B; and at S=4 on 32,768 B

speed_8192B._about: alice29, LIMIT=8192 default. Speedup is against S=1 in the same run.

size_dependence._about: The load-bearing claim: does the cost shrink with SEGMENT LENGTH? Same S=4, same corpus, 4x the segment length.
size_dependence.reading: 4x the segment length cut the penalty 2.29x. The direction is confirmed with the real implementation.
size_dependence.pilot_did_not_replicate: The scratch pilot measured this same step as 8.9% -> 2.6%, a 3.5x reduction. The shipped implementation measures 9.08% -> 3.97%, a 2.29x reduction. The 8 KB figures agree to 0.2 points; the 32 KB one is 1.4 points worse than the pilot claimed. Quote 3.97%.
size_dependence.two_costs_are_conflated_here: At both sample sizes the segments (560 and 2,221 tokens) are SHORTER than LIMIT=8192, so a segment never fills its context window. The measured penalty therefore mixes two effects: one cold start per segment, and less available context per segment. On a file large enough that each segment exceeds LIMIT, only the first applies. That predicts the penalty keeps shrinking - but it is a PREDICTION, and trap 3 exists because this project keeps promoting those to findings.
size_dependence.not_extrapolated: Two points are a direction, not a curve. enwik8 at S=16 would give ~1.7M token segments, ~766x longer than the 32 KB test. Do not compute what the penalty would be there - measure it.

lockstep_decode.what_this_unblocks: Long_Time_Tests 3.1, a verified full-enwik8 round-trip, was costed at 17 days and declared infeasible, blocked behind multi-week int8 determinism work. At S=16 decode measured 10.59x. That is roughly a weekend, and it needs no int8 at all - the largest single blocker on the roadmap, removed by ~130 lines.

speed_32768B._about: Measured 2026-08-23, recorded here 2026-08-31 - previously only in RANK_3_REPORT.md. alice29, LIMIT=8192, round-trip ok at every S. bpb is deterministic and matches the S=1/S=4 rows already recorded under size_dependence; the B/s figures are from a different sitting and are not comparable with the 8,192 B table.
speed_32768B.penalty_decay: Same S, 4x the segment length: S=4 9.08% -> 3.97% (2.29x), S=8 19.25% -> 7.61% (2.53x), S=16 37.41% -> 13.52% (2.77x). Three S values now agree that the cost tracks segment length, which is a curve rather than the single direction size_dependence had.

thread_count_is_part_of_the_format._about: Found by the 2026-08-31 thread sweep, which recorded output size per run. It is a bigger result than the sweep it fell out of.
thread_count_is_part_of_the_format.observation: 16,384 B at S=8 encodes to 2,209 B at 4, 6 and 8 threads and 2,210 B at 12 and 20 - consistent across all three passes. Different size means different bytes.
thread_count_is_part_of_the_format.cross_decode_before_the_fix: Silent corruption, not an error. A blob written at 12 threads and read at 6 returned 8,692 bytes for an 8,192-byte input; written at 6 and read at 12 returned 8,320. No exception was raised in either direction - the token COUNT in the header is right, so the decoder runs to completion and hands back plausible-looking garbage.
thread_count_is_part_of_the_format.fix: The thread count is now a header byte, and _apply_threads restores it at decode. Self-healing rather than fail-loud because it can be: torch.set_num_threads AFTER the model is loaded does take effect here and reproduces a byte-identical stream (verified against a true 12-thread blob). It is still checked afterwards, since that is an OpenMP build detail rather than a promise, and raises with the exact LLM_PTC_THREADS value to set if it did not apply.
thread_count_is_part_of_the_format.verified: Cross-decode ok in both directions after the fix (6->20 and 20->6). Round-trip ok at S=1,2,4,8,16 on 4,096 B, and the sequential path is still 515 B, unchanged.
thread_count_is_part_of_the_format.format: Header is now n(4) | S(1) | threads(1) | segment sizes(4 x S) | blobs. Second format change today, after logits_to_keep - both are recorded and neither is backward compatible.
thread_count_is_part_of_the_format.not_extended_to_the_sequential_path: Deliberate. results.json already records sequential output as byte-identical across 6 and 20 threads at 3 KB, cross-decoding both ways. That is 'safe for the sizes tested', not proven - but it is measured, and this change is scoped to the path where corruption was actually observed.

memory_ceiling._about: Computed 2026-08-31 from the model config (30 layers, 3 KV heads, head_dim 64, float32).
memory_ceiling.consequence: S=16 does not fit. This box is 15.7 GB with ~2.4 GB typically free, so the practical setting for any run long enough to slide is S=8 - 9.36x decode instead of 14.11x. The logits_to_keep fix removed a separate 12.0 GiB allocation on the same code path; it was necessary, not sufficient.
